Fraxtor co-invests in Greater Osaka’s UIB Konan Phase 3 in first JV with listed REIT
article:
Fraxtor said on Aug 26 that it has closed fundraising for its co-investment in UIB Konan Phase 3, a logistics development in Greater Osaka, Japan. The transaction marks Fraxtor’s first joint venture with a listed REIT and its continued expansion into Japan’s logistics sector.

The offering, which was open to accredited and institutional investors, comprised Singapore-dollar and Japanese-yen tranches. Both were oversubscribed, according to the Singapore-based fractional real estate investment platform.

Fraxtor will co-invest alongside SGX Mainboard-listed UI Boustead REIT (UIB REIT) through a joint venture vehicle. UIB Konan Phase 3 is the third and final phase of UIB Konan Logistics Park in Konan City, Shiga Prefecture.

Looking to invest in overseas properties ? Explore projects available for sale around the world

Entities within UIB Holdings, the sponsor of UIB REIT, will act as the project's development manager and asset manager.

The development is the third and final phase of UIB Konan Logistics Park, and comprises two logistics facilities with a combined gross floor area of about 48,139 sq m (518,168 sq ft) on a 53,349 sq m (574,302 sq ft) site. Located within the Greater Osaka logistics corridor, the site is within 2km of the Ritto Konan Interchange and has direct access to National Route 1.

Greater Osaka’s logistics vacancy rate stood at 2.2% in 1Q2026, the lowest among Japan’s four major metropolitan markets, according to Fraxtor.

“Japan’s logistics sector continues to be underpinned by strong structural tailwinds, from persistent undersupply of modern facilities to resilient occupier demand in key metropolitan corridors,” says Oliver Siah, co-founder of Fraxtor.

title: Tata Power loses US$490 mil arbitration challenge in Singapore
article:
(Aug 26): Tata Power Co, one of India’s largest non-state power producers, lost a challenge to a US$490 million arbitration award for violating an agreement with an investor to bid for a coal asset in Russia and denying it the opportunity to benefit.

The Singapore International Commercial Court rejected the Indian company’s challenge to the quantum of the damages awarded to Kleros Capital Partners, as well as its claim that the majority order was a breach of natural justice, according to a copy of the order delivered Wednesday.

The origin of the case dates back to 2013, when Kleros approached Tata Power with a proposal to jointly bid for a Russian coal deposit it estimated to contain reserves worth US$1.1 billion. The two companies entered into a non-disclosure agreement effective through four years starting September 2013.

However, in 2015, the relationship began to sour, with disagreements over who would lead the bid as well as the ownership structure of the proposed project, the court document said. The relationship ended the next year.

As a result, Kleros didn’t bid for the mine in federal auctions in Russia in December 2017 and wound down its operations in the country. Tata Power submitted a bid in the auction through a Russian unit and won the mining licence when the non-disclosure pact with Kleros expired. It later surrendered the licence after finding the project unviable.

See also: Jurong Island ‘great’ place for co-located industry and nuclear power, says MIT nuclear scientist

Kleros dragged Tata Power into arbitration, arguing that the Indian firm “had breached the NDAs by misusing the confidential information disclosed thereunder and by acting in bad faith in excluding Kleros from the project”.

The court agreed with Kleros and rejected Tata Power’s challenge on all counts, keeping the arbitral award unchanged and imposing costs on the company, the amount of which currently remains undecided.

title: ST Engineering given $750 mil MRT contract in Taiwan
article:
ST Engineering has been given a $750 million rail services contract in Taiwan.

The contract is for the Taoyuan MRT Green Line Extension, part of a broader contract with consortium partner Hyundai Rotem.

Earlier this month, ST Engineering said its order book has hit a record of $35.7 billion.

For this Taiwan contract, ST Engineering will lead overall project management and systems integration, and provide a suite of rail electronics solutions including supervisory control and data acquisition, communications system, automatic fare collection system and platform screen doors.

Hyundai Rotem, the partner, will provide the power supply system and rolling stock.

Project execution is scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026 and will be delivered over seven years.

See also: Penguin International wins newbuild contract from Singapore navy

“This win reflects our customer’s confidence in our ability to deliver large-scale rail infrastructure programmes, underpinned by our longstanding commitment to supporting Taiwan’s rail development," says Gareth Tang, ST Engineering's president for its urban solutions segment.

"We appreciate the opportunity to contribute to the Taoyuan MRT Green Line Extension and will draw on our experience and strong local expertise to ensure a smooth execution,”

The 7.2km Taoyuan MRT Green Line Extension, with five stations, forms part of Taoyuan's broader rail development plans to enhance connectivity across the city.

See also: Kingsmen wins $30 mil contract to build NS-theme gallery

The extension will improve access to major residential, commercial and transport hubs and enable connections with Taiwan’s wider rail network when completed.

ST Engineering shares closed at $10.58 on Aug 26, down 1.21% for the day but up 25.8% year to date.

title: Thomson Medical's net loss for FY2026 narrows 40.8% y-o-y
article:
Thomson Medical Group has narrowed its net loss for its FY2026 by 40.8% y-o-y to $27.8 million.

The bottom line was partly weighed down by an impairment of $15.2 million on its hospital in Vietnam, to reflect "changes in prevailing macroeconomic and market conditions in Vietnam and the resulting revision of assumptions used in the impairment assessment."

Revenue for the year ended June was up 6.4% to $420.1 million as the company managed stronger underlying operating performance, ranging from higher revenue intensity to contributions from new segments and also higher patient volumes.

EBITDA for the year was up 23.3% to $67.3 million. Thomson Medical benefitted from lower financing costs as well, down 15.4% to $47.4 million.

Thomson Medical says Malaysia was a particularly strong contributor during the year, with revenue increasing as it continued to scale its oncology and specialist services.

This reflects the increasing contribution from capabilities that Thomson Medical has invested in building across its regional healthcare platform.

See also: Avi-Tech, citing challenging semiconductor and electronics industry, reports net loss of $1.4 mil for FY2026

"We entered FY2026 focused on translating the investments we have made into stronger operating performance," says group CEO Dr Melvin Heng.

"Our expanded specialist capabilities in Malaysia are gaining momentum, our Singapore business continues to benefit from higher-value care and greater pricing discipline, and patient volumes are growing in Vietnam.

"These are important building blocks as we move towards generating more sustainable earnings from the platform we have built," adds Heng.

See also: Micro-Mechanics' FY2026 earnings up 28.3%; aims to double revenue come by FY2031

Going forward, Thomson Medical will remain focused on strengthening execution and improving operating leverage across its regional portfolio.

In Singapore, this includes expanding its network of specialist and multidisciplinary services and strengthening insurance partnerships.

In Malaysia, Thomson Medical will continue to build on the growing contribution from oncology and other specialist services, while progressing its longer-term plans in Johor.

In Vietnam, FV Hospital will continue to expand its capabilities and capacity to meet growing demand for specialised care.

Thomson Medical shares closed at 5.4 cents on Aug 26, up 1.89% for the day but down 10% year to date.

title: Avi-Tech, citing challenging semiconductor and electronics industry, reports net loss of $1.4 mil for FY2026
article:
Avi-Tech Holdings has reported a loss of $1.4 million for its FY2026, reversing from earnings of $0.7 million in the year earlier. Revenue was down 15.3% to $18.3 million, "reflecting softer demand" across the semiconductor and electronics industries.

The company will not pay a dividend for FY2026.

Avi-Tech warns that industry conditions will remain challenging over the coming months as subdued demand, heightened competition, and ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties continue to weigh on the semiconductor and electronics industries.

It will continue to monitor market developments closely while maintaining financial discipline and operational resilience.

Tan Xianyang, who took over as the executive chairman after buying $17 million worth of shares from Lim Eng Hong at 33 cents each, calls FY2026 a "challenging" year for the semiconductor and electronics industry.

The deal was completed in May.

See also: Micro-Mechanics' FY2026 earnings up 28.3%; aims to double revenue come by FY2031

"As we navigate the group’s next phase, we will remain focused on preserving our financial strength, deploying our resources prudently, and positioning Avi-Tech for sustainable long-term growth and value creation," he adds.

Avi-Tech shares closed at 20 cents on Aug 26, up 5.26%.

title: Micro-Mechanics' FY2026 earnings up 28.3%; aims to double revenue come by FY2031
article:
Micro-Mechanics (Holdings) has reported earnings of $5.27 million for its 4QFY2026 ended June, a jump of 65.7% y-o-y. This brings its full-year earnings to $15.9 million, up 28.3%.

Revenue for the year was up 15.8% to $75.5 million, driven mainly by its consumable tools segment, although wafer fabrication equipment sales increased as well.

The company plans to pay a final dividend of 3 cents, which will bring total payout for FY2026 to 6 cents, representing a payout ratio of 52.4%.

Over the coming five years to 2031, Micro-Mechanics plans to double its revenue to $150 million.

In addition, the company plans to maintain its gross profit margin of more than 50%, and to limit overhead costs to less than 20% of its revenue.

See also: ISOTeam's 2HFY2026 earnings down 49% y-o-y; full year dip of 4.5%

Micro-Mechanics plans to hit these targets by boosting operations at markets such as China and Malaysia to better support customers.

It will also invest in next-generation equipment and processes. Capex is seen to increase to $12 million in the current FY2027 versus $3.8 million in the last financial year.

Micro-Mechanics shares closed at $2.79 on Aug 26, down 0.71% for the day but up 71.17% year to date.

title: ISOTeam's 2HFY2026 earnings down 49% y-o-y; full year dip of 4.5%
article:
ISOTeam has reported earnings of $1.6 million for its 2HFY2026, down 49% y-o-y. This brings its earnings for the full year ended June to $4.9 million, down 4.5%. Revenue for the full year dropped by 11.3% to $105.7 million, which the company explains is because of timing of recognition.

Despite the weaker bottomline, ISOTeam plans to pay a final dividend of 0.11 cents per share, up from 0.08 cents paid this time last year.

Anthony Koh, executive director and CEO explains that ISOTeam "prioritised quality of earnings over topline growth."

"While revenue moderated in line with the timing of project completions across our core segments, we are encouraged that gross profit margin strengthened to 18.3%, mainly because of cost savings from housing some of our workers at the converted space within our head office.

"Looking ahead, our $185.3 million order book and Singapore's sustained investment in upgrading its public housing estates position ISOTeam well to capture opportunities in the built environment sector over the coming years," adds Koh.

ISOTeam shares closed at 6.9 cents on Aug 26, down 2.82% for the day, extending a drop of 13.75% year to date.

title: Australia gets states’ buy-in for AI data centre energy rules
article:
(Aug 26): Australia’s government secured a broad agreement with regional leaders on developing new data centres but appears to have set aside a demand that they be powered by renewable energy.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a deal Wednesday on a national AI development plan, with new legislation to be introduced early next year. However, Canberra appears not to have forced his government’s earlier renewables demand after two regions opposed it.

Queensland Premier David Crisafulli, who praised the deal struck on Wednesday, had argued that it should be left to his state government to choose how to supply electricity to data centres as it owns the whole power system.

“We believe that we can control our data sovereignty, protect the rights of local communities and enable that energy mix to bring those data centres on,” Crisafulli said after the meeting with Albanese and the leaders of the other states and territories. He added that his state and the Northern Territory, which had also opposed the initial plan, differed from the rest of the country in this respect.

The Queensland energy minister’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment sent outside normal business hours.

“If there is surplus then that of course could be available” for data centres, Albanese told journalists after the meeting, speaking about Queensland and the Northern Territory, which we said were “in different positions from other states".

See also: Australia to enforce power, water standards for data centres

“We came to a common position, which recognises that all states aren’t exactly the same and that was accommodated in the way that we normally do, in a flexible way,” Albanese said.

In its initial announcements on the national AI policy over the past few months, the federal government had touted a policy where data centre operators would be required to pay for their own energy supply. Energy Minister Chris Bowen said earlier this month that “data centres are welcome if they bring their own additional renewable energy,” threatening to legislate to enforce that standard nationally.

The federal and state governments will now work together “to develop consistent mandatory standards for data centre energy, water and land use, and support skills and training opportunities", according to a statement released after the meeting.

See also: Singapore awards 200MW of data centre capacity across four existing operators

Australia is in the middle of a rapid buildout of AI data centres, attracting investment due to its abundant land and strong renewable energy capabilities. Companies invested almost A$9 billion on data centres and servers in the first three months of this year.

Queensland has earmarked land for a more than 700ha data centre and tech hub run by a Singapore-based developer. The project is estimated to cost more than A$30 billion and tipped to be the largest of its kind in Australia, according to a recent report from the national broadcaster ABC.
